Strait of Hormuz Status: October 5, 2026 | Straits Daily Brief

Strait of Hormuz · Daily brief · UTC
5 October 2026 .
Brent $ 100.21 -1.85 % · Transits 1 (2026-09-27) · AI-assisted
01 TradeWinds News reports Iran has hit 11 ships in one week in the Strait of Hormuz, with Jalopnik reporting a US official says Iran's targeting capabilities keep improving.

02 Brent stood at $100.21, down 1.85% over 24 hours, as of 23:51 UTC; IMF PortWatch recorded 1 transit on 2026-09-27, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day.

Situation
The Strait of Hormuz remains under severe pressure. TradeWinds News reports 11 ships have been hit in one week, and Jalopnik, citing a US official, reports that Iran's targeting capabilities keep improving. gCaptain reports that UK Maritime Trade Operations documented five separate incidents on Monday alone, including four tanker attacks and a separate incident in which an IRGC warning was issued. gCaptain also reports that an IRGC patrol ordered a vessel to turn back or face targeting, a claim TradeWinds News and gCaptain both carry. On the physical transit picture, Iran says the strait will not reopen until conditions are met, while Hellenic Shipping News reports Iraq's state tanker firm is moving crude through the strait, leaving the two positions in tension. Iraqi Oil Tankers Co. is also seeking to purchase vessels to route crude beyond the strait entirely, per Hellenic Shipping News. Saudi Aramco CEO Amin Nasser, speaking at the Energy Intelligence Forum in London, said global oil inventories have fallen to scarily thin levels, per Hellenic Shipping News. Brent stood at $100.21, down 1.85% over 24 hours, as of 23:51 UTC. IMF PortWatch recorded 1 transit on 2026-09-27, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day. The site's indexed event count stands at 51 in the last 24 hours. As of 23:50 UTC, 224 AIS-visible vessels were holding position away from berth in the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf watch box, a count that leaves out ships within 25km of a working port. On the Hormuz Index, Crisis Pressure, the state composite, sits in the extreme band, flat over 24 hours, with its value set by physical transit deviation alone; the Escalation Forecast sits in the elevated band, rising over 24 hours, with the Brent-WTI forward spread as its top contributor.
